title: Function map a published Discussion paragraph
stimulus: Take one Discussion paragraph from a paper you have read this month. Do not choose one you already find confusing.
task: Label every sentence with exactly one function: context, gap, aim, method, observation, comparison, interpretation, mechanism, qualification, limitation, implication. Then state the paragraph's single claim in one sentence WITHOUT using 'and'. If you cannot, mark where the second claim begins.

title: Ten verbs against their evidence
stimulus: Ten sentences from your own drafts that contain: show, affect, relate to, prove, find, have, make, demonstrate, confirm, establish.
task: For each: (a) name the evidence type behind it, (b) place that evidence on the claim ladder in references/epistemic-calibration.md, (c) choose the strongest verb that rung licenses. Do not soften everything reflexively — one or two should probably get STRONGER.

title: One sentence, one job
stimulus: Find the three longest sentences in your most recent draft.
task: For each, list the scientific jobs it performs. Split so that each sentence does one. Reorder so every sentence opens with something the previous sentence established.

title: Hold the terms still
stimulus: A paragraph of your own containing at least four instances of 'this', 'these', or 'it'.
task: Attach a noun to every bare demonstrative. Then list every term used for each entity and pick one. Finally, check whether any term means something different in the last sentence than in the first.

title: Results from a figure: growth curves
stimulus: Figure: OD600 growth curves for wild-type and three mutant strains, n=4 biological replicates, shaded 95% CI. The delta-spoIIIAE strain plateaus at OD 0.62 versus 0.94 for wild type (p=0.003, Welch's t-test at 8 h). The other two mutants overlap the wild-type curve.
task: Write a 100-150 word Results paragraph. Report what was measured, which groups were compared, direction, magnitude, uncertainty. No mechanism, no significance-to-the-field, no speculation. Every sentence must be one that could only be wrong if the measurement were wrong.

title: Results from a figure: a negative result
stimulus: Figure: co-immunoprecipitation blot. Bait protein pulls down a known partner (positive control lane, strong band) but no band is detected for the candidate protein across three replicates. Input lanes confirm the candidate is expressed. Detection limit was not formally determined.
task: Write the Results paragraph. The hard part: report the negative result at exactly the strength the experiment supports, and make the reader able to see what the experiment could and could not have detected.

title: Same figure, now the Discussion
stimulus: Use your Results paragraph from fig2res-01.
task: Write a 150-200 word Discussion paragraph: restate the finding without replaying the numbers, interpret it, make the reasoning explicit, name one alternative explanation, state what remains uncertain, and end on what should be tested next. Before submitting, read your first and last sentence side by side and check that the certainty has not risen.

title: Argument table: coevolution to interaction
stimulus: Claim under construction: SpoIIIAA and SpoIIIAE form part of the transenvelope channel. Available evidence: an AlphaFold-Multimer prediction with high interface pTM, and a coevolutionary signal between residues in the two proteins.
task: Build the table: claim | evidence | reasoning | what the evidence cannot establish. Write the reasoning column as full sentences — these are the sentences that will be missing from your paragraph if you skip this step. Then write the paragraph.

title: Argument table: crossing a scale
stimulus: Claim under construction: the mutation impairs sporulation efficiency in the host. Available evidence: a purified-protein assay showing reduced ATPase activity, and a plate-based sporulation assay in a laboratory strain.
task: List every level of organisation the claim crosses (molecule, protein complex, cell, strain, species, natural environment). For each crossing, write either the evidence that bridges it or the assumption you are making. Then write the paragraph with the assumptions visible.

title: Four rival explanations
stimulus: Your own preferred interpretation of any result you currently believe.
task: Write one alternative biological explanation, one methodological explanation, one sampling or statistical explanation, and one experiment that would distinguish between them. Then rank: which rival is genuinely hardest to exclude? Say so in the paragraph.

title: Direction of time, boundary of population
stimulus: A cross-sectional dataset: gene expression and phenotype severity measured in the same samples at one timepoint, correlation r=0.61.
task: Write the Discussion paragraph. Every ordering word ('precedes', 'leads to', 'downstream', 'initiates') must be either justified by the design or removed. State explicitly which set the claim covers.

title: Abstract reconstruction
task: 250 words maximum, in seven moves: background, gap, aim, methods, principal result (concrete, with a number), interpretation, significance or limitation. Then check: does the aim match the methods, do the results answer the aim, does the last sentence exceed the evidence, and has any quantifier grown between the result and the conclusion?

title: Rebuild one Results subsection
stimulus: One subsection from your dissertation, report, or manuscript.
task: One finding per paragraph. Numbers before interpretation. No mechanism unless directly tested. No 'interesting', 'important', or 'novel' without a stated comparison. Stable terminology throughout. Submit for a sentence-by-sentence boundary audit.

title: Rebuild one Discussion subsection
stimulus: The Discussion subsection corresponding to own-results-01.
task: Seven moves per paragraph: main finding, interpretation, reasoning, comparison with prior literature, alternative explanation, limitation, implication or next experiment. The reasoning move is the one you skip — write it first, before anything else in the paragraph.

title: Full argument map and reviewer simulation
task: Map: research question, hypothesis, method, observation, interpretation, alternative explanation, conclusion, validation requirement. Mark every arrow where a reader must supply a step you have not written. Then request the reviewer simulation: three major comments, three minor, one strongest aspect, one central threat to validity, one question you must be able to answer before submission.
